conflicts.point: Whether mandatory human review and personal legal sign-offs for final decisions meaningfully prevent discrimination or merely create inefficient barriers that disadvantage new market entrants.

positions.stance: Mandatory human review and personal legal accountability are necessary institutional safeguards against systemic bias, even if they introduce administrative friction.
Mandatory human review imposes bureaucratic friction that protects legacy incumbents, slows economic throughput, and harms job seekers.

conflicts.point: Whether decentralized open-source model audits and proxy-variable stripping can effectively remove systemic bias without requiring centralized bureaucratic intervention or named human signatories.

positions.stance: Decentralized open-source audits and telemetry provide faster, more effective bias correction than manual compliance reviews.
Technical scrubbing of model parameters and open-source audits fail to alter recursive feedback loops and structural financial exclusion.

verdicts.conflict: Whether mandatory human review and personal legal sign-offs for final decisions meaningfully prevent discrimination or merely create inefficient barriers that disadvantage new market entrants.
verdicts.rationale: Safetyists emphasize legal accountability voids, while accelerationists stress bureaucratic drag on market entrants. Neither camp provides comprehensive data measuring the trade-off between prevented discrimination incidents and delayed economic transactions.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Longitudinal studies tracking error rates and compliance costs across regulated versus unregulated automated hiring pipelines would tip the balance.

verdicts.conflict: Whether decentralized open-source model audits and proxy-variable stripping can effectively remove systemic bias without requiring centralized bureaucratic intervention or named human signatories.
verdicts.rationale: While accelerationists cite an 18 percent increase in thin-file credit access via proxy stripping, skeptics demonstrate that commercial entities routinely block independent oversight through proprietary restrictions. This critique exposes a structural gap in decentralized audit models that relies on vendor self-reporting.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Legislative mandates requiring mandatory open-source audit access with verified independent oversight could validate technical scrubbing frameworks.
